essence:
Continuing from the yogin's perception (V2-B): how can one cognition be *known by
another* cognition (jñāntaravedyatā)?

The other's cognition, being self-luminous, shines of itself; the yogin's cognition, by the excess of
purity and its un-opposed spreading, knows it without the other's self-ness being hidden.
The relation of object-and-holder does not hold between two cognitions.
